subject: general
question: Which component in an MCB is responsible for detecting a short circuit?
solution:
The correct answer is __Solenoid**(Option 2)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The solenoid__ is the component in an MCB responsible for detecting a short circuit.
 
• When a short circuit occurs, a large current flows through the solenoid.
 
• This generates a magnetic field, which triggers the tripping mechanism.
 
• The solenoid ensures the MCB trips instantly to prevent damage to the system.
 
• Unlike the bimetallic strip used for overload protection, the solenoid handles short-circuit conditions.
 
• It is designed to react quickly to high fault currents.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Arc chute:**
 
 
• The arc chute is used to extinguish the arc formed during the opening of contacts.
 
• It ensures the safe interruption of current.
 
 
 
• **Bimetallic strip:**
 
 
• The bimetallic strip is used for overload protection.
 
• It bends due to heat generated by excessive current, triggering the trip mechanism.
 
 
 
• **Handle:**
 
 
• The handle is used to manually reset or operate the MCB.
 
• It does not play a role in detecting faults.
 
 
</ul
